A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OCM research, and their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison. V1's Appendices A and B correspond to v2's Appendices A.1 and A.2; v2 adds substantial further material.

before.justification: V1 reports original covariance-estimation errors and DDPM/DDIM sampling results on a two-dimensional nine-Gaussian mixture, evaluated using MMD in Figure 1.

after.justification: V2 retains the toy experiments and reports original image-generation, likelihood, recall and computational-cost results, including Tables 3–5, 8, 11 and 12.

M1.justification: The Hessian-diagonal regression objective, single-Rademacher-sample training approach, covariance construction and skip-step DDPM/DDIM updates are retained. V2 documents shared-backbone prediction heads and practical image-sampling details, but does not establish a revision of the existing OCM algorithm.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates only the nine-Gaussian toy distribution and leaves image modelling to future work. V2 retains that task and adds CIFAR10, CelebA 64x64, LSUN Bedroom, ImageNet 64x64 and class-conditional ImageNet 256x256 generation using latent diffusion.

E2.justification: V2 introduces NPR-DDPM/NPR-DDIM as important comparators in the image likelihood and FID experiments. Within the retained toy DDIM comparison, Figure 3d removes the beta-DDIM, iDDIM and True-DDIM curves present in v1 Figure 1d. Ana/A-DDPM and NS/SN-DDPM are matched as renamed methods.

E3.justification: The stated toy training budget and MMD kernels remain unchanged. New image experiments introduce linear/cosine schedules, pretrained image models, NLL upper-bound evaluation, FID on 50,000 generated samples, recall, classifier-free-guidance sweeps and time-adjusted comparisons at approximately FID 6. These are added protocols, rather than demonstrated changes to the original toy setting.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained toy analyses, v2 adds Rademacher sample-count sensitivity studies (Figures 1 and 5), guidance-dependent quality/diversity analysis (Figure 4 and Table 11), parameter and inference-overhead measurements (Table 8), and qualitative sample studies across sampling settings (Appendix C.4).

E5.justification: V1 provides no repeated-run counts or uncertainty summaries. V2 Appendix C.2 reports three evaluation repetitions with different seeds, and Table 9 provides means and percentage-scaled standard deviations for OCM likelihood and FID results. This documents repeated evaluation, not three independent training runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive likelihood, FID, recall, runtime and qualitative image results, while largely retaining the toy trends and removing three toy DDIM result curves. For example, its new Table 11 reports ImageNet 256x256 FID/recall of 5.33/46.58% for OCM-DDIM versus 6.12/41.15% for DDIM at 10 steps and CFG=2.0. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over corresponding v1 image results.

T1.justification: The original covariance identity and optimality proof are retained, but v2 strengthens Theorem 2 with an upper-bound statement and Jensen-based derivation. New Appendix A.3 develops second-moment identities and proves Theorem 3: OCM-DDPM and SN-DDPM recover identical optimal diagonal covariances under an exact score and optimal training.

C1.justification: V1 claims improved covariance estimation and DDPM/DDIM sampling efficiency, with image applications deferred. V2's abstract, introduction and conclusion add claims about likelihood, recall/diversity and scalability across pixel-space and latent image generation, substantially broadening the asserted contribution.

C2.justification: V2 adds a likelihood-versus-FID trade-off interpretation, acknowledging that SN-DDPM or NPR-DDPM can outperform OCM on individual metrics. It attributes SN-DDPM's likelihood difficulties to quadratic-term error amplification and links learned covariance to diversity. Appendix B.1 also qualifies the computational-efficiency discussion with measured overhead, including 11.2% on LSUN Bedroom.

D1.justification: Beyond v1's brief toy optimizer settings, v2 supplies a code-access link, pretrained-model sources, shared-backbone and prediction-head specifications, parameter counts, GPU hardware, AdamW training budgets, batch sizes, checkpoint selection, EMA, covariance clipping and evaluation details (Section 3.3 and Appendix B). These substantially expand reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: V1 primarily positions OCM among covariance estimators. V2 adds substantial positioning against numerical solvers, Schrodinger bridges, GAN hybrids and diffusion distillation, with new references such as Peebles and Xie and Salimans and colleagues. Section 6 also relates OCM to likelihood-sensitive sampling, compression and future video applications.

P1.justification: V2 revises the title and extensively rewrites the introduction, separates background into its own section, adds a dedicated training/inference subsection, and separates broader related work from the conclusion. It reorganizes the original proofs within Appendix A and introduces a structured appendix contents page and experimental sections.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. The original overview table and toy figure are relocated and revised, while v2 adds algorithm boxes, extensive benchmark and uncertainty tables, guidance plots, architecture/runtime tables and image grids. These materially change the visual presentation beyond renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V1's practical validation rests entirely on a toy distribution and explicitly defers image modelling. V2 addresses that central limitation with pixel-space and latent image experiments, supported by computational measurements, three-seed evaluation summaries, expanded theory and detailed reproducibility information. Some reporting inconsistencies remain, notably Table 10's 256x256 caption versus its 64x64 experiment text, and advantages are setting-dependent. Nevertheless, the added validation and transparency substantially improve overall quality.
